meta.title: Ondra Speech-to-Text
meta.description: Speech-to-text with local Whisper first and cloud as a fallback, producing text with millisecond timestamps (handbook §1.5, P1, reuse tier). The handbook names three things and this package handles each honestly: timestamps are produced and normalised to integer milliseconds; local-first is honoured and the fallback can be switched off; speaker separation cannot be done and is therefore not faked. Neither whisper.cpp nor whisper-1 performs diarisation, so the speaker field exists, stays empty when unknown, and diarized is always false. No invented labels like speaker-1: recording the user's words as hers is an attribution error, which hurts more than forgetting. On the local path the audio is first checked for 16 kHz mono WAV; if it is anything else it is transcoded with ffmpeg, and if ffmpeg is missing the original file is still tried once, because some builds carry their own decoder and giving up early would decide for the user. Three judgements are hard-wired: first, anything that can be transcribed on this machine never leaves it, because a voice clip carries timbre, mood and the television in the background; second, failures are silent, logged at debug with counters only, never interrupting the conversation; third, nothing is invented, so a failure returns a reason code and an empty string rather than placeholder text, since placeholders become things the user supposedly said. Outbound still passes privacy, with allow, ask and deny kept distinct; without privacy the cloud path is refused. This package creates no tables, writes no memory, assembles no prompt and draws no UI; ingestion belongs to O-128, outbound compliance to O-076, and the interface to the application shell.
